title: Django ORM: models, queries and migrations

videos.script: Lesson 3 kept registrations in a Python list. Restart the server, and they are gone. Send two at once, and both can take the last seat. {{list}} Today they move into PostgreSQL, and the database becomes the source of truth. {{postgres}} You install PostgreSQL 16 from Ubuntu, make a role and a database, and point agenda at them. Each step that you skip has its own error message, and you will read all four. {{fails}} Then the models. A Python class becomes a table, and a migration is the history of how it got there. You read the SQL before it runs. {{models}} You ask for rows with QuerySets, and you watch the SQL they become. Building a query costs nothing. Using it sends exactly one statement. {{sql}} And then the experiment this lesson is built around. Twenty people try to register for a workshop with twelve seats, at the same instant. Without a lock, all twenty get in. With one line that locks the event's row, twelve get in and eight are refused. {{race}} Last, the loop that sends one query per row, which hides on every list page, and the single query that replaces it.
